dimensions.assessment: Affects all consumers of targeted food and beverage products, food and beverage manufacturers, online retailers, children under 13, and multiple federal agencies.
dimensions.evidence: requires health warnings on labels and in advertisements for food and beverages that are sweetened, processed, or contain a high level of certain nutrients of concern, and it prohibits specifically advertising such products to children.

dimensions.assessment: Imposes broad regulatory requirements on food packaging and marketing practices nationwide, alongside significant federal research and public education programs.
dimensions.evidence: Unless its label includes the following statement: Food and Drug Administration Warning: Drinking beverages with added sugar can contribute to obesity, type 2 diabetes, and tooth decay.

importance_detail.rationale: The Childhood Diabetes Reduction Act of 2026 mandates front-of-package warning labels and nutrient disclosures for numerous food and beverage products, restricts advertising of these products to children under the FTC, authorizes appropriations for HHS ($5 million/year for labels plus unspecified sums), NIH ($60 million/year for research), and CDC ($10 million/year for education), and restores FTC rulemaking authority on children's advertising.

summary: The Childhood Diabetes Reduction Act of 2026 requires specific health and nutrient warning labels on certain food and beverage products, such as sugar-sweetened items, products with high-intensity sweeteners, ultra-processed foods, and items high in nutrients of concern like added sugar, saturated fat, or sodium. It restricts marketing and advertising these products to children under 13, restores the Federal Trade Commission's authority to regulate children's advertising, and expands nutrition science research through the National Institutes of Health and public education campaigns.

affected_groups.effect: Must add specific warning labels to the front packaging of qualifying products, include warnings in advertisements, and comply with restrictions on marketing to children.
Will be protected from child-directed marketing and advertising for targeted food and beverage products.
Gains enforcement powers over violations regarding child-directed advertising and labeling disclosures, along with restored authority to regulate children's advertising.
Tasked with expanding research programs on nutrition science and conducting public education campaigns regarding nutrition and physical activity.
affected_groups.group: National Institutes of Health (NIH) and CDC

key_provisions: Requires front-of-package FDA warning labels on sugar-sweetened beverages, products with high-intensity sweeteners, and ultra-processed foods, stating specific health risks and that they are not recommended for children.
Requires front-of-package 'High in' warning labels on foods containing high levels of nutrients of concern, such as added sugar, saturated fat, or sodium.
Prohibits marketing or advertising these labeled foods and beverages in a manner that reasonably appears to be directed at children under the age of 13.
Requires advertisements for these products to include the relevant mandatory health or nutrient warning labels.
Expands National Institutes of Health programs and research regarding nutrition science and the health effects of ultra-processed foods.
Directs the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to conduct or support public education activities concerning nutrition, physical activity, and diet-related chronic disease.
Repeals restrictions on the Federal Trade Commission's statutory authority to promulgate rules on children's advertising.
missing_information: Specific funding amounts authorized for fiscal years 2027 through 2031 for HHS and the FTC to promulgate regulations and carry out enforcement activities under Section 101.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Childhood Diabetes Reduction Act of 2026 requires specific health and nutrient warning labels on certain food and beverage products, such as sugar-sweetened items, products with high-intensity sweeteners, ultra-processed foods, and items high in nutrients of concern like added sugar, saturated fat, or sodium. It restricts marketing and advertising these products to children under 13, restores the Federal Trade Commission's authority to regulate children's advertising, and expands nutrition science research through the National Institutes of Health and public education campaigns.
summary_detail.significance: The bill impacts food and beverage labeling and marketing nationwide by enforcing mandatory health warnings for processed and sweetened foods, restricting advertising targeting children, and increasing federal funding for nutrition research and education.
